guideTitle: 6 Best Floor Lamps with Remote Control (2026)
metaTitle: Best Floor Lamps with Remote Control (2026)
metaDescription: Six floor lamps with remote control compared on brightness, memory, timers and backup switches, so you can adjust the light from your chair or bed.
introParagraphs: A remote turns a floor lamp from something you reach for into something you adjust from your chair. The six lamps here use that idea differently. The GERGO pairs a torchiere with an adjustable reading light for a combined 2100 lumens, the SIBRILLE torchiere reaches 1800 lumens from 30W, and the Coucrek runs a 9W bulb with a one hour timer and memory.

Backup controls and extras set them apart. The GOEBLESON has a magnetic remote and a foot switch on a 64.4 inch slim pole, the Beanliss is an arc lamp with a heavy anti-tipping base, and the Luvkczc is a 69 inch torchiere with three metal shelves. Most also include a rotary knob or foot switch for when the remote is lost.

We evaluated each lamp on remote design, backup controls, brightness, stability and extras, based on product specs and buyer feedback. For active adults and the family members shopping for them, we favored lamps whose remote is simple, stays with the lamp and is backed up by a physical switch.

products.name: GERGO Torchiere Floor Lamp with Remote and Reading Light

specList.label: Control
specList.value: Remote or rotary switch, each light separate

products.description:
The GERGO combines a torchiere and an adjustable reading light, powered by 11W and 7W LED bulbs that together reach 2100 lumens. Both bulbs are included, and each light can be controlled individually through the remote or a rotary switch. That flexibility lets you run the reading light alone or add room light.

The pairing suits a chair where you read and relax in turns. The tradeoff is that the reading light is modest in output, and having two lights means two things to adjust. It sits in the upper-middle of the cost range.

The rotary switch is a useful backup if the remote goes missing. Compared with the SIBRILLE, it has less total output but adds a reading light. It is the most versatile remote lamp in the group.
products.bestFor: A reading chair that needs both room light and a focused light, each adjustable
pros: Torchiere and reading light controlled separately
Both LED bulbs included for 2100 lumens
Rotary switch as a remote backup
cons: Two lights mean more to adjust

products.name: SIBRILLE 72 Inch Torchiere LED Floor Lamp
products.description:
The SIBRILLE is a 72 inch torchiere with 30W, 1800 lumens, and dimming from 10 to 100 percent. The color range runs from 3000K to 6500K, and a remote or button controls it. The large shade throws light upward to the ceiling, creating a broad, even glow.

Its height and shade size make it a room lamp rather than a reading lamp. The tradeoff is it is the highest on the cost scale, and the 10 percent dimming floor is higher than some rivals. It is also tall, so it needs a stable spot.

The lamp is rotatable, which helps direct the light. Compared with the GERGO, it has more room light but no separate reading light. It is the pick for filling a large room.
products.bestFor: Large rooms that need a tall, even uplight with remote control
cons: Dimming only goes down to 10 percent
Tall 72 inch size needs a clear spot

products.name: Coucrek Torchiere Floor Lamp with Magnetic Remote
products.description:
The Coucrek is a torchiere with a 9W dimmable LED bulb, stepless dimming from 10 to 100 percent, and adjustable color. It remembers your last brightness and color settings and offers a one hour timer. The magnetic remote sticks to the pole, and a rotary switch gives a backup.

Memory means you rarely need to reset it, which is ideal for daily use. The tradeoff is that 9W is moderate output, so it suits smaller rooms. The 10 percent dimming floor is also higher than the lowest-dimming rivals.

It is easy to live with and sits at the lower-middle of the cost range. Compared with the GOEBLESON, it adds memory and a rotary backup. It is a good everyday lamp.
products.bestFor: Daily use where a lamp that remembers its settings saves effort

products.name: Beanliss Arc Floor Lamp with Remote
products.description:
The Beanliss is an arc floor lamp with a dimmable LED, three color temperatures and fully adjustable light direction. The included remote lets you adjust from across the room, and a timer is available. Its heavy metal base is designed to resist tipping.

The arc reaches over a chair, so the base stays out of the way. The tradeoff is that arc lamps take up more floor area, and the listing does not give an exact lumen figure. It sits in the mid-range of cost.

For a sofa or recliner, the reach and the heavy base are a strong combination. Compared with the Coucrek, it points light where you need it but lacks memory. It is a good pick for a seating area.
products.bestFor: Sofas and recliners where the light must reach over the seat
pros: Arc reach hangs light over a seat
cons: No lumen figure stated on the listing

products.name: GOEBLESON 64.4 Inch Slim Floor Lamp with Magnetic Remote
products.description:
The GOEBLESON is a slim 64.4 inch lamp with a magnetic remote and a foot switch. It offers a dimmer and a timer, and the remote, bulb and batteries are included. It is the lowest-cost lamp in the group.

The slim profile fits into a corner, and the magnetic remote sticks to the pole so it stays with the lamp. The tradeoff is simplicity: the listing gives few details on brightness, and the lamp is better for ambience. It is a good starter lamp.

Compared with the Coucrek, it is cheaper but lacks the memory function. It is a sensible choice for a bedroom.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and corners on a tight budget
pros: Magnetic remote stays on the pole
cons: Few brightness details on the listing

products.name: Luvkczc Torchiere Floor Lamp with 3-Tier Shelves
products.description:
The Luvkczc is a 69 inch torchiere with three metal shelves, a remote and adjustable color temperatures. Its open-top design directs light upward to fill the room. The shelves give you a place for books, plants or decorative items.

The shelves make it two pieces of furniture in one, which is practical in a small room. The tradeoff is that the shelves add weight to a tall pole, so it needs a stable spot, and loading them unevenly could be a tipping risk. It is lower in cost.

Compared with the SIBRILLE, it is shorter and offers storage. It is a good pick for a reading nook.
products.bestFor: A reading nook that needs light and a little shelf space
cons: Shelves raise tipping risk if overloaded
Taller pole needs a stable spot

buyingCriteria.explanation: A remote should be easy to grip and work from your chair. The GOEBLESON and Coucrek have magnetic remotes that stick to the pole, which keeps them from getting lost. Range matters less than reliable operation, but check that it works through furniture. Look for large, clearly labeled buttons.

Remotes lose batteries and go missing, so a rotary switch or foot switch is important. The GERGO and Coucrek offer rotary switches, and the GOEBLESON has a foot switch. Physical buttons also beat touch sensors, which can fail with dry skin. Always check there is a manual option.

A lamp that remembers its last brightness and color saves daily fiddling. The Coucrek has memory and a one hour timer, and the Beanliss offers a timer. Timers are useful for bedtime reading. Choose these extras if you read before sleep.

Reading wants roughly 400 to 800 lumens on the page, and a living room wants 1000 or more. The GERGO reaches 2100 lumens in total, the SIBRILLE 1800 lumens, and the Coucrek's 9W bulb is lower. Aging eyes often need more light, so choose output with a dimmer. Check the listing for lumens.

A base at least 8 inches across and weight low in the pole reduce tip-over risk. The Beanliss has a heavy anti-tipping base, while the Luvkczc's shelves add weight higher up. Avoid placing tall lamps where they might be bumped. Route cords away from walking paths.

Warm 2700K to 3000K suits relaxing, 3500K to 4000K suits general tasks, and 4000K to 5000K suits focused reading. The SIBRILLE spans 3000K to 6500K and the Beanliss offers three settings. A CRI of 80 or more is a living-space minimum. Adjustable color suits mixed use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Remote and backup controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at remote design and whether each lamp has a manual backup. The Coucrek and GOEBLESON have magnetic remotes, and the GERGO has a rotary switch. A lamp with both remote and manual control scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brightness and bulbs
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated output, from the GERGO's 2100 lumens and the SIBRILLE's 1800 lumens to the Coucrek's 9W bulb. We also noted which lamps include bulbs. Lamps with enough output ranked higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Memory, timers and extras
howWeEvaluated.description: We rewarded memory, timers and useful extras like the Luvkczc's shelves. The Coucrek's memory and timer stood out. The most basic pick, the GOEBLESON, has fewer extras.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered base design and weight, including the Beanliss's heavy base and the Luvkczc's shelves. The strongest overall pick, the GERGO, has a stable torchiere design. Stable lamps reduce tip-over risk.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared features against each lamp's relative cost tier. The GOEBLESON is the lowest cost, and the SIBRILLE the premium pick.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A timer, memory and a low, warm setting. A remote you can find in the dark helps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Coucrek has a one hour timer and memory, and the Beanliss offers a timer. The GOEBLESON adds a timer at the lowest cost.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want strong output and a separate reading light, as the GERGO offers, or the big room fill of the SIBRILLE. Backup controls and bulbs included add value.

cards.text: You need a simple bedroom lamp. The GOEBLESON is the lowest cost, and the Luvkczc adds shelves at a modest tier.

faq.q: Which remote floor lamp is best overall?
faq.a: The GERGO is the best overall because it combines a torchiere and reading light, both bulbs included, with a remote and rotary switch. The SIBRILLE is better for very large rooms. Pick by how you sit and read.

faq.q: What if I lose the remote?
faq.a: Choose a lamp with a rotary or foot switch backup. The GERGO and Coucrek have rotary switches, and the GOEBLESON has a foot switch. A magnetic remote that sticks to the pole is harder to lose.

faq.q: Do remote lamps need special batteries?
faq.a: Most use common coin or button cells, and the GOEBLESON includes batteries. Check the listing before buying. Replace them when the response slows.

faq.q: Does the remote work from another room?
faq.a: Range varies, and walls reduce it. Test from your usual seat. Keep the remote within reach of your chair.

faq.q: Are shelves on a lamp safe?
faq.a: They can be, but shelves add weight high on the pole. Place light items on the Luvkczc's shelves and keep them evenly loaded. Avoid putting it where it might be bumped.

faq.q: How bright should the lamp be?
faq.a: Aim for 400 to 800 lumens on the reading surface and 1000 or more for room light. The GERGO reaches 2100 lumens in total. A dimmer lets you lower it when needed.

faq.q: Can I use a smart plug with these?
faq.a: Some lamps may work with a smart plug, but check the listing and that the lamp turns on at power-up. A manual switch should remain on. A remote lamp usually already covers your needs.
